newsitem.title: UK: UK to shake up overseas telecoms market - FT.
newsitem.headline: UK to shake up overseas telecoms market - FT.

text.p: Britain is set to make its largest single move towards opening up its international telecommunications market to competition, the Financial Times newspaper reported on Wednesday.

Licences will be given to all 46 companies seeking to compete with British Telecommunications and Cable & Wireless unit Mercury Communications in offering a full range of telecoms services between Britain and the rest of the world, it said.
The licences will be effective from January 1.
To date companies other than BT and Mercury have only been able to operate by leasing lines from one of the two British companies.
The newspaper said the move could entice substantial inward investment but might also result in a significant fall in the UK's overseas telecoms revenues.
The decision might also defuse opposition by AT&T the largest U.S. long distance carrier, to the proposed $20 billion takeover by BT of MCI Communications, it said.
AT&T argued the deal should be blocked by the U.S. authorities because the UK market was not yet fully open.
The list of applicants for the international licences include AT&T, Eurotunnel and Globel One -- the alliance between Deutsche Telekom and France Telecom.
"All are expected to be approved and the Department of Trade and Industry wants to issue the licences in a single block before the Christmas break," the FT said.
